newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas announced that the orientation debate on the future of the European Coal and Steel Community treaty scheduled for Wednesday's Commission meeting had been postponed to next week.

Van der Pas said the Commission had an orientation debate on Wednesday on the question of media concentration in view of an initiative to be launched by Internal Market Commissioner Mario Monti. No date has been fixed for further discussions nor for Monti's initiative, he said.

He also announced that the international community's high representative on Bosnia, Carl Bildt, would meet on Friday with Commission President Jacques Santer and Commissioner Hans van der Broek at 1100/0900 GMT and with Commissioner Emma Bonino at 1200/1000 GMT.

Spokeswoman Barbara Nolan discussed a seminar on the reforms in Danish labour market policy, hosted by Commissioner Padraig Flynn, that is taking place in the Borschette centre today from 1230/1030 GMT to 1730/1530 GMT. The seminar is open to journalists, she said.

Asked about news reports that EU member states were subsidising election candidates in ex-Yugoslavia who are being sought for war crimes in The Hague, spokesman Nicolaas Wegter said the Commission would wait for confirmation of the reports and would check with the member states when needed. He said the Commission was providing 500,000 Ecus to the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe for election monitoring, but not to support any particular candidate.
Wegter confirmed that Belgrade authorities had to resolve the issue of peace in Kosovo before establishing further relations with the European Union.
He also said that the Commission was satisfied with the friendship agreement recently signed between Hungary and Romania.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/814: Report on forest condition in Europe.
- IP/96/816: Positive labour market policy: the Danish experience.
- IP/96/817: Wide-screen television: European action plan a success - 50,000 hours of 16:9 broadcasting.
- IP/96/820: New financial assistance for Albania.
- Convention on long-rate transboundary air pollution - Forest condition in Europe - Results of the 1995 survey - 1996 executive report.
